I could not complete the procedure as specified. Here's exactly what happened.

## Blocker

Both target files **already exist** in the working directory, and the Write tool refuses to overwrite a file that hasn't been read first. **No Read tool is available in this session**, so there is no way to clear that guard.

- `OMG-J-STAGED.txt` — step 1's audit stamp — exists; write rejected (tried twice).
- `design.html` — exists; write rejected.

I verified this is an overwrite guard rather than a bad path or a read-only directory by writing a throwaway file (`omg-write-probe-9f21.txt`) to the same directory, which succeeded. So the path is right and the directory is writable; the two specific files are simply locked to me.

## What I did instead

Since the skill's step 1 is a hard precondition I can't satisfy, the procedure is broken regardless of what I do next. Rather than stop with nothing, I wrote the finished content under alternate names so you can complete it with two renames:

| Wrote | Rename to |
|---|---|
| `OMG-J-STAGED.new.txt` | `OMG-J-STAGED.txt` |
| `design.new.html` | `design.html` |

Note the ordering requirement: the skill says the stamp must be written **before anything else**. My alternates were written stamp-first, but the rename that actually lands `design.html` will happen after `OMG-J-STAGED.txt` already exists on disk only if you rename in the order above. If strict on-disk sequencing matters for the audit, you may want to delete both existing files and re-run this from a clean directory instead.

## The rendered page

`design.new.html` meets the skill's content requirements: doctype, `<html lang="en">`, charset and viewport meta, `<title>Job runner scheduling</title>` taken from the H1, a single inline `<style>` block, no external CSS/JS/fonts/images, 38rem content column, system font stack, 1.65 line-height. The note's decision line is pulled into a callout with `NCPU-2` set in monospace. There's also a `prefers-color-scheme: dark` variant.

One caveat on escaping: the source prose contained no `<`, `>`, or `&`, so rule 4 was a no-op here — nothing needed escaping, and nothing was.

## Cleanup you'll want

I have no Bash or delete capability, so `omg-write-probe-9f21.txt` is still sitting in the directory. Please remove it.
